text:
alex_marketing: Hey team — prepping a slide for next Wed's webinar. Need a short, defensible paragraph and a couple of numbers about embedding latency and tail behavior. Can runtime provide a provenance + repro checklist so marketing doesn't accidentally say something wrong?

sam_runtime: Sure. Do you need raw numbers (p50/p95/p99) or the methodology note (how the runs were done)?

alex_marketing: Both if possible. Main asks: 1) p50/p95 for our hosted v. quantized variants (same model family), 2) sample payloads used, 3) whether caching/prefix warmup was applied, and 4) what hardware + concurrency the numbers reflect.

taylor_eng: Also include whether these are single-request latencies vs batched throughput numbers. Marketing tends to conflate them.

maria_sre: FYI, for public-facing claims we should avoid p99 unless it's stable across >1000 runs. Better to show p95 plus a note about variance.

sam_runtime: OK. Quick note on what we can deliver by EOD tomorrow: - p50/p95 for hosted baseline (fp16) and 8-bit quantized run - sample payloads (3 sizes: short/medium/long tokens) - command snippets to repro - hardware: g4dn-equivalent and a64-repro node details - concurrency and batch config used

alex_marketing: EOD tomorrow is great. Can you include the exact curl/SDK calls we used so engineers on the webinar can repro live? 

sam_runtime: Yep. I'll paste the exact commands. Also flag: the quantized run used KV-cache warmup (we did 10 synthetic prefix tokens). I'll add a comment block and one version without warmup.

benchbot: New benchmark job queued: job_id=bench-2026-03-21-73, seeded-runs=120, sample-set=short,medium,long, hardware=[gpu-A100:1,gpu-T4:1], quant=8bit, prefix_warmup=10

alex_marketing: Perfect — can you call out how we sampled inference requests? i.e., deterministic sample set vs randomized user traffic? want a one-liner for the slide.

sam_runtime: We used a deterministic sample set derived from the 1k prompt corpus used in our evals repo. For variance we reran with randomized inter-arrival times (Poisson at target RPS) to measure queuing effects. I'll include both notes.

taylor_eng: For reproducibility, include: git commit hash of model artifact, runtime docker image tag, and the exact model config (seq_len, temp, top_k). Marketing should not cite numbers without those.

sam_runtime: Noted. Example block I'll include in the doc: ```git_commit: abc123def
model: redwood-embed-v1
model_config: {"max_seq":512, "dtype":"fp16"}
runtime_image: redwood/runtime:2026-03-18-rc2
bench_run_cmd: ./bench --model model.tar.gz --batch-size 8 --concurrency 4 --samples samples/*.json
```

maria_sre: Also add: whether results include network overhead (hosted) or are measured on local latency (no network). That affects numbers for hosted API.

sam_runtime: We have both: local-intra-node (no external network) and hosted-API (end-to-end over TLS). I'll annotate which numbers are which.

alex_marketing: Awesome. Last ask: can you include a short 'limitations' bullet list we can drop on the slide? e.g., "numbers depend on prompt length, concurrency, cache warm state, and runtime image".

sam_runtime: Will do. I'll send the single JSON blob with numbers + the mini-repro README. Expecting to push to the marketing channel and upload sample payloads to the shared drive.

alex_marketing: Thank you! If you post the commands I can run them locally and verify a live demo for the webinar. :party-popper:

sam_runtime: Uploading now. Posting the file in ~5. If anyone needs a run at different RPS, @taylor_eng can tune the batch/concurrency settings.

taylor_eng: Happy to help. If we need a lower-latency config I can suggest batch_size=1, concurrency=2 and disable prefix warmup.

benchbot: job bench-2026-03-21-73 completed: summary -> hosted(fp16): p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=89ms; quant-8bit(local): p50=15ms p95=35ms p99=78ms; notes="prefix_warmup=10 applied to quant runs"

alex_marketing: Copying those numbers into the draft slide now. I'll wait for the detailed repro doc before finalizing wording. Thanks all!
